Rootzén, J. and Johnsson, F. (2017). Managing the costs of CO2 abatement in the cement industry. Climate Policy 17(6), 781-800 (published online 2016). doi:10.1080/14693062.2016.1191007. Held as the Chalmers author pre-print.

Region: Nordic countries (DK, FI, NO, SE). Loaded: the average Nordic cement plant (C0, Table 4 cost breakdown, fuel and electricity use, emissions), the new BAT kiln (C1), the post-combustion MEA kiln with a CCGT for regeneration steam (C2, kiln_dry-precalciner_ccs-diffuse) and the full oxy-combustion kiln (C3, kiln_oxy-fuel) from Tables 3, 5 and 6: fixed operating cost, total production cost (cost-levelized), specific emissions, captured CO2 and avoidance cost. All costs 2010 EUR per t CEMENT (clinker ratio 0.8). C2 and C3 costs INCLUDE CAPTURE (not split). In _other-values: variable cost and annualised capital per kiln, the C2 energy penalty (2400 MJ/t cement), CO2 transport and storage (25 EUR/t CO2), the Table 12 cement cost increases (C2 +61% excluding carbon cost, +90-95% with it; C3 +39%/+65-70%) and the downstream result (building cost up <1%). Not loaded: concrete and building cost model (Tables 7-11, Figs 5-8). Traps: (1) Table 4 note c gives thermal use as 3650 MJ/t cement, but the per-carrier requirements sum to 2.9 GJ/t cement = 3650 x 0.8, so 3650 is per t clinker; the sum is loaded; (2) Table 2 labels the oxy-combustion kiln C2, a typo for C3; (3) Table 12 footnotes swap high and low carbon price; the values follow the row labels (low 40, high 100 in Period 1). Locator: pre-print page numbers.
